mcat_description.short: A portable pantry is a prefabricated, relocatable cabin structure designed for food preparation, storage, and serving, sold as a complete unit with built-in kitchen fittings. It is manufactured primarily from mild steel or FRP panels and supplied as a ready-to-install modular unit.
mcat_description.long: Portable pantry cabins are prefabricated modular structures built on a mild steel base frame, with insulated wall and roof panels, designed to function as a self-contained kitchen or canteen at temporary or semi-permanent sites. They are equipped with built-in amenities such as cooking ranges, sinks, wash basins, storage cupboards, exhaust systems, and electrical fittings, making them immediately operational upon installation. These cabins are widely deployed at construction sites, industrial campuses, mining camps, corporate office premises, and disaster relief areas where a permanent kitchen structure is not feasible. Customisation in size, material finish, and internal fittings is standard practice, with manufacturers offering both standard catalogue sizes and bespoke builds to client specifications.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Portable Pantry' refers specifically to a prefabricated, relocatable cabin structure used as a kitchen, canteen, or food preparation unit — distinct from furniture-type pull-out pantry cabinets. The dominant construction material is mild steel (MS) framing with insulated wall panels (PUF, EPS, or glass wool), though FRP and PVC panel variants are also commercially available. Manufacturers are concentrated in Maharashtra (Thane, Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Dombivli), Rajasthan, Telangana (Hyderabad), and Karnataka (Bengaluru). The primary buyer is a construction contractor, industrial plant operator, or corporate facility manager procuring a temporary or semi-permanent food service facility. Customisation is standard — buyers specify size, internal fittings (cooking range, sink, storage, exhaust), insulation grade, and colour. The term 'portable canteen cabin' is used interchangeably with 'portable pantry cabin' across the Indian market. Container-based conversions (20ft/40ft shipping containers) represent a premium sub-segment. Structures are quoted per piece for standard sizes and per sq ft for custom builds.
